name: authors-evolution-delivery
description: Evolutionary architecture and continuous delivery principles. No text reused.

rules.title: Fitness functions protect the characteristics the design claims
rules.requirement: For each characteristic the design claims to protect, such as latency or coupling, there is an automated check named that would fail if a change violated it.

source.name: Neal Ford
source.locator: Building Evolutionary Architectures, Chapter 2, Fitness Functions

rules.title: Every change reaches production through one automated pipeline
rules.requirement: The design names the pipeline that builds, tests and deploys the service, states that no manual step alters the artifact, and shows that the same artifact is promoted through environments.

source.name: Jez Humble and David Farley
source.locator: Continuous Delivery, Chapter 5, Anatomy of the Deployment Pipeline

rules.title: Decisions are recorded with context, options and consequences
rules.requirement: Each significant decision has a record stating the context, the options considered, the choice, the consequences, and its status, so that it can be revisited later with the reasoning intact.

rules.title: Feature flags have an owner and a removal date
rules.requirement: Each flag used for rollout or kill switches names an owner and when it will be removed, so flags do not accumulate as permanent branches.

rules.title: Decisions are deferred to the last responsible moment where cheap
rules.question: Which of the decisions in this document could be deferred until more is known, what would it cost to keep that option open, and why are you deciding now?

source.name: Mary and Tom Poppendieck
source.locator: Lean Software Development, Chapter 3, Decide as Late as Possible
